orientation.heading: s0ma in one minute
orientation.lead: Three things to know before anything else:
paragraphs: s0ma is a way of writing software so that the software carries an accurate description of itself.

You write `.s0ma` files. In them, every part of your program first says what it is for, what it needs and what it promises, and then gives its code. s0ma turns those files into ordinary Python, and beside the Python it keeps a record of every part. You, your program, and your coding agent can all ask that record questions, and get answers that come from the program itself instead of from a document somebody hoped to keep up to date.

points.because: Everything in the build directory is written by s0ma and rewritten every time you build.
When the answer is "nothing", you write `none`. Leaving a required line out is an error.
points.say: Every line is a question, and every question gets an answer.

points.because: `s0ma check` reads your files, changes none of them, and tells you what is wrong and how to put it right.

page.preview_note: A version marked `(preview)` is the latest release together with the changes made since, which are not released yet.
page.summary: One page to find your way around s0ma: what the parts of a `.s0ma` file are, what each line of them means, the commands you will use most, and where to ask for more.
page.title: s0ma quick reference

reading.heading: How to read the tables
reading.holds_lead: **Holds** says what kind of answer the line takes.
reading.imports: An import is written `json` for a whole package, `datetime:date` for one name out of a package, and `numpy as np` to give it a shorter name.
reading.lead: Each declaration below has a table with one row for each line you can write, in the order you would write them. s0ma's own messages call these lines *fields*.
reading.long_forms: Two longer forms are there when a line gets crowded. For long text, write `|` in place of the text and put the text on the lines underneath, further in. For a long list, put one item on each line underneath, each starting with `- `.

may.means: "There is nothing here", said out loud: `raises: none`.
"Not decided yet", with the reason in quotes: `expects: pending("waiting for the pricing rules")`. Day to day this is a warning. In `strict` and `release` mode it is refused until you answer.
The line needs a real answer.

reading.may_lead: **May also be** says what the line may hold in place of a real answer.

write.means: Write the line only in the situation its row describes.
Leave it out whenever you like.

reading.write_lead: **Write it?** says whether the line has to be there.

rules.detail: Never edit anything in the build directory. If a generated file is changed by hand, `s0ma verify` reports it and `s0ma build` refuses to go on until the change is moved into the `.s0ma` file it belongs to.
and the file's name matches the module's name. Names have no dots in them: join a feature and its layer with an underscore, as in `library_domain`.
rules.rule: Every file opens with a `module` header,

rules.detail: `intent` is on every declaration, and it gives the reason, not a description of the code.
rules.rule: Every part says why it exists.

rules.detail: Write `none` when there is nothing to say and `pending("reason")` when you have not decided. Do not leave the line out.

A line s0ma cannot read is reported, never passed over: a name it does not know, or a line that starts in the wrong place. Day to day these are warnings. In `strict` and `release` mode they are refused.
rules.rule: Spell and indent each line exactly.

rules.detail: A nerve's code is one `def`. A `SERVICE` or an `ADAPTER` may be a `class` instead.
Outside code goes in the header's `requires`. Parts of other s0ma files go in `uses`. An example is the one exception.
and a file only reaches the layers its own layer allows.
A part listed in `exports` is `PUBLIC`. A part that is not listed is `INTERNAL` or `TEST`.
It already links a part to the errors in its `raises` line and to the types its code mentions, so those need no `axon` and no `depends_on` line.
rules.rule: Do not write a connection s0ma works out for itself.

rules.detail: The function's name decides whether the test runs. One the test runner would never run is reported, because it would still count as a check on the parts it names.

rules.rule: When you change the code, change its description in the same edit,

rules.detail: `exec`, `eval`, `__import__`, or code that swaps another part's behaviour while the program runs.

shape.heading: What a file looks like
notes: A file opens with one `module` header. After it come as many declarations as you like, in any order.
Inside a declaration the description comes first and the code comes after, with a line of exactly three hyphens between them.
Each line of a description starts with exactly four spaces. A line that belongs to the line above it, as in a block, goes further in.
A note to a reader starts with `#` and sits on a line of its own. Written after an answer, on the same line, it is read as part of the answer and refused.
The file is named after its module: `module library_domain` lives in `library_domain.s0ma`.
project: library/                          one folder for each feature
library_domain.s0ma           one file for each layer the feature needs
build/                                written by s0ma: never edit
library_domain.py                 the Python made from your file
library_domain.s0ma.json          the record of what your file declared
docs/                             the pages your doc-ref and doc-guide produce
